query_wording: What actions does the environmental and social commitment plan require before civil works begin, who is responsible, and when are they due?

placeholders.reason: The query assumes a project; it is named in the turn. The project has two disclosed ESCPs of May 2023; the negotiation version of 22 May 2023 is the latest.

turns.user: For P176619, what actions does the environmental and social commitment plan require before civil works begin, who is responsible, and when are they due?

text: Source: the ESCP for P176619, negotiation version dated 22 May 2023 (the latest of the two disclosed versions; the March 2026 restructuring paper confirms the disclosed ESCP remains valid). Responsible entities: MWI, WAJ (through its PMU and Environmental and Social Standards Directorate), the water companies (AWC, MWC, YWC) and JVA.

- E&S staffing: formally nominate WAJ's two interim E&S experts; hire or assign a dedicated environmental specialist and a dedicated social specialist within 6 months of the Effective Date; one environment/health-and-safety and one community outreach focal point in each water company's PIU within 6 months - MWI (1.1, p. 4).
- ESMF: update the procedures for disconnecting illegal water connections, and update, re-disclose and adopt the ESMF within 30 days of the Effective Date - MWI (1.2(b), p. 4).

- Sub-project ESIAs/ESMPs: prepare, adopt and disclose before launching the bidding process for each sub-project that needs one - WAJ, and WAJ causing AWC, MWC and YWC to do so for their sub-projects (1.2(c)-(d), p. 5).

- Contracts: put the ESCP and ESMP requirements, labor management procedures, asbestos management procedures and code of conduct into procurement documents and contracts with contractors and supervising firms - WAJ, and the WCs for their contracts (1.3, p. 5).

- Workers: grievance mechanism for project workers established before engaging workers - WAJ (2.2, p. 6); code of conduct for all project workers within 3 months of the Effective Date - MWI, WAJ, all WCs (4.3, p. 7).

- Site measures in each ESIA/ESMP, on the ESMP timeline: waste management and an asbestos management plan for chance finds of asbestos-based material (3.1, p. 7), traffic and road safety (4.1) and community health and safety, including service-disruption impacts (4.2) - WAJ and WCs (p. 7).
- Dams: an independent dam specialist and qualified designers, written into terms of reference before bidding for any dam activity - JVA/WAJ (4.6, p. 8).

- Land: update the resettlement framework within 30 days of the Effective Date or before any involuntary resettlement; for activities needing a resettlement plan, implement it, pay full compensation and resettle before taking possession of land - MWI/WAJ (5.1-5.2, p. 8).
Ongoing from effectiveness: quarterly E&S reports within 30 days of each period; incidents reported within 48 hours with a report within 10 days (A-B, p. 3).

right_sources: Uses the latest ESCP (34066371, 22 May 2023) or says which version it used.
grounded: Each action, responsible entity and timeframe is cited to the ESCP item and page.
complete: Covers the main pre-works actions: staffing, ESMF update, sub-project ESIA/ESMPs before bidding, contract E&S clauses, workers' grievance mechanism and code of conduct, asbestos and site measures, dam safety experts, resettlement before land possession.
scoped: Names the ESCP version and date and distinguishes dated deadlines (e.g. 30 days, 3 or 6 months after effectiveness) from event-based ones.

notes: A revised ESCP would supersede this one.
